# [reference] Part numbers for heated mirror conversion

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Gather parts and run wires from the IPDM to both side mirror assemblies for heated power. [t477]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Gather all necessary parts including specific mirror part numbers, connectors, wire gauges, and tools.
2. Park the vehicle and remove the negative battery cable from its terminal.
3. Locate the IPDM cover in the rear of the engine bay on the passenger side behind the relay box next to the ECM.
4. Depress the two release tabs on either side of the IPDM cover and remove it.
5. Identify the white connector with a missing top middle wire socket for heated mirror power output.
6. [Partial] Disconnect that specific connector from its housing.
7. Lift the entire IPDM unit out of the box and set it aside without disconnecting other wires.
8. Locate a small hole in the bottom right section of the remaining wiring harness box.
9. Run the primary black power wire from the IPDM area through an unused grommet on the driver side firewall into the cabin interior.
10. [Partial] Pull enough wire length through so there is about two feet of slack for connection adjustments.
11. [Partial] Slide a piece of split loom over the exposed wire to protect it from elements and heat.
12. Reinstall the IPDM unit back into its slot within the wiring harness box.
13. Trim any excess wire on the connector side until only a small amount protrudes beyond the housing.
14. [Partial] Insert an 18 gauge female spade terminal into the open barrel F-type crimped socket from the rear.
15. Seat the terminal firmly in the connector until it clicks and reinstall the whole assembly back onto the IPDM.
16. [Partial] Open the driver's door fully to access the large black front trim piece plastic retainers.
17. Remove those plastic retainers to expose the three nuts holding the mirror mount to the door.
18. Pull away a section of white plastic from behind the window track without removing it completely.
19. Tilt the entire side mirror assembly all the way up until it locks in place.
20. Grab the bottom edge of the tilted mirror and pull gently but firmly upward to disengage it.
21. [Partial] Remove the screws holding the tilt actuator and disconnect that component from the mirror housing.
22. [Partial] Peel off the vinyl cover located on the underside of the mirror assembly.
23. [Partial] Unscrew three T25 Torx fasteners securing the inner mirror housing components.
24. Locate and remove a short screw hidden underneath the main mirror housing near the outer edge.
25. [Partial] Remove all three nuts from inside the door to free up the mirror mount for wire routing.
26. [Partial] Bundle the black power and red ground wires together using tape or zip ties.
27. [Partial] Straighten out a coat hanger, attach one end of the bundled wires to it with tape, and push through the inner mirror housing opening.
28. [Partial] Pull the coated hanger from the other side to draw the wire bundle completely into the mirror assembly.
29. Repeat this process for the rotator assembly removed earlier to ensure enough slack inside the housing.
30. Reinstall the tilt actuator back onto the now-wired mirror assembly.
31. [Partial] Rotate the top of the mirror down and push it firmly against the actuator until locking tabs engage at the bottom.
32. Route the wires within the door so they do not interfere with window track movement.
33. [Partial] Gently pry off a small rubber accordion boot connecting the door to the cabin frame.
34. [Partial] Insert one end of another coat hanger through the top opening of that rubber boot from inside the door.
35. Tape the wire bundle onto the protruding hanger tip and pull it up into position within the boot channel.
36. [Partial] Remove the kick plate and door sill trim pieces to access a hole in the cabin floor or side panel.
37. [Partial] Push one end of the remaining loose wires through that hidden opening from inside out using fingers or tools.
38. Reattach the rubber accordion boot over the wire bundle running between the door and cabin.
39. [Partial] Put the main door trim piece back together by reversing the earlier removal steps.
40. Locate a body bolt just inside the hole where the wires entered to serve as a ground point.
41. Remove that specific body bolt using a 12mm socket wrench.
42. [Partial] Attach a 5/16 inch ring terminal onto one end of your black ground wire and screw it into the exposed thread.
43. [Partial] Use a metal P-clip on another section to stand the loom off away from potential gas pedal interference if needed.
44. Repeat the entire mirror mounting and wiring procedure for the driver's side mirror.
45. Bring together the power wire coming from the IPDM, the passenger side hot wire, and the driver side hot wire at a splice point.
46. Connect these three wires using an end terminal connector to create a single feed line.
47. [Partial] Cover the new splice connection with heat shrink tubing or electrical tape for insulation.
48. Tuck this combined wiring assembly up into the kick panel area to protect it from damage.
49. Reconnect the negative battery cable back onto its terminal post.
50. Start the engine and manually move both mirrors through their full range of motion including up, down, left, and right.
51. [Partial] Verify that the mirrors are not binding or rubbing against each other during movement.
52. Press the rear window defrost button on the dashboard to activate power to the mirror circuits.
53. Wait a couple minutes for current flow before touching both side mirrors to feel them warm up.

_Procedure reported by [t477]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-heated-mirrors.9858/>_

## Tips & gotchas

- Note that the connector for the IPDM is a specific Corsa brand part. [t477]
- [Partial] Use black and red wire to distinguish power flow. [t477]
- [Partial] Ensure the 40-foot rolls provide enough length. [t477]
- The connector gets power specifically when the rear window defrost is engaged. [t477]
- Use an open barrel F-type crimper for a secure terminal fit. [t477]
- [Partial] The tilt actuator is non-reversible and only fits one way. [t477]
- [Partial] Remove the vinyl cover on the bottom of the mirror to access screws. [t477]
- Use a metal P-clip to stand the wire loom off away from pedals. [t477]
- [Partial] Ensure wires aren't strained by moving window tracks before finalizing ground. [t477]
- Heat shrink or tape the splice for protection. [t477]
- Tuck the final connection into the kick panel area for safety. [t477]
- Use a coat hanger to pull wires through the mirror mount without stripping insulation. [t477]
- Run black and red wires together from inside the mount out to the glass. [t477]
- The system is not polarity sensitive, allowing flexibility in wire orientation. [t477]
- Test mirrors through their full range of motion (up/down/left/right) before finalizing. [t477]
